name: Blood Orange Crown Break
description: A traditional 330ml can stands in a shallow granite tank of blood-orange juice where a halved fruit struck 18 milliseconds ago, throwing a genuine asymmetric Worthington crown. The backdrop is a second tank of the same juice lit from behind, so the whole set glows through real liquid with suspended pulp rather than a painted gradient.
lighting: Backlit juice wall, hard grid sparkle, flash-frozen
subject: product
prompt: a traditional 330ml can, 66mm across and 115mm tall with a necked-in shoulder and a bare mill-finish aluminum seam at top and base, standing in a honed black-granite tank holding a 90mm bed of blood-orange juice, crimson in mass and glowing orange where thin, a halved blood orange having struck the surface 18 milliseconds earlier and thrown a genuinely asymmetric crown — a torn liquid sheet necking into ligaments then into unequal droplets, never a symmetric radial burst, the impact cavity not yet collapsed, backlit through a second tank of the same juice standing 2.4 metres behind with visible suspended pulp specks and slow-rising bubbles inside it so the field glows white-hot orange at its core through scarlet to oxblood at the corners, eight warm practical bulbs spaced on a bar 1.2 metres behind the can rendering as soft orbs that clip to cat's-eyes toward the frame corners, a gridded strip softbox camera-right raking a broad graded sheen down the can and a second strip behind it drawing one bright edge line, a hard gridded head above throwing real caustics onto the granite, hand-cut clear ice with internal feather fractures and melt-rounded corners, condensation run-tracks, the honed stone returning only soft foreshortened reflections offset from each contact point and at least three stops darker, never a mirrored copy, the hard reflection living on the juice surface instead, no rendered text or logos anywhere, professional flash-frozen beverage-campaign realism
